transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-07-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Derrick Huang (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Singh (CTO - Lyon), Marco Alvarez (Head of Infra), Ellie Carter (Security)
Summary: Intro and qualification focused on Private/VPC deployment options, VPC peering vs PrivateLink/private endpoints, region constraints (APAC requirement), network egress controls, KMS/HSM, SOC2 and audit logs. Agreed next steps around sharing security artifacts, VPC details, and follow-up infra deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava from redwood, i'll kick us off, um quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: priya here, cto, we run internal gen-ai for clinical summarization, big on data residency and audit trails
[00:16] Marco: marco, infra, we manage aws accounts, vpc, networking, and seg controls
[00:21] Ellie: ellie, security and compliance, focusing on encryption and log retention
[00:25] Derrick: derrick from redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll do the more technical bits today
[00:29] Ava: great, main thing on the agenda - private deployment, we support private vpc deployments and a private control plane option, want to understand your constraints, timeline, and success criteria

[02:00] Priya: timeline is about q4 pilot, production maybe q1, um key constraints - we need all PHI to stay in our vpc, no model artifacts leaving, and we need region in ap-southeast-2 ideally, because of regulatory preferences

[03:12] Marco: question on connectivity - are you doing classic vpc peering, transit gateway, or private endpoints? what's the recommended pattern?

[03:25] Derrick: yeah great q. so we support a few options: 1) VPC peering for direct routing between customer vpc and our managed serving subnets; 2) AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints so control plane and data plane don't traverse public internet; 3) Transit Gateway if you want hub-and-spoke at scale. each has trade-offs - peering is simpler but doesn't scale across multiple accounts/regions as well; privatelink gives you endpoint ENIs in your subnet and is our typical enterprise recommendation for isolation

[04:05] Marco: ok, if we go privatelink, how do you handle DNS and split-horizon? we have internal-only hostnames for services and want to avoid leaking to public route53

[04:17] Derrick: we usually provision interface endpoints in your VPC and provide a private DNS option or you can keep it disabled and paste the endpoint ip/eni in your internal resolver. some customers leverage Route53 private hosted zones. there's a doc/terraform snippet we'll share.

[05:10] Ellie: from security perspective we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, plus syslog/flow logs for peering endpoints, can you confirm

[05:24] Derrick: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for data at rest and for S3 key wrapping, and we can push audit logs and access logs to an s3 or to your logging account via cross-account delivery. flow logs and VPC flow are your side but we can provide recommendations for capturing traffic to the interface endpoints

[06:02] Priya: region question - you mentioned ap-southeast-2, are your private nodes available there? we can't route traffic out to us-west-2 for any PHI processing

[06:18] Ava: currently we have private deployment packages in a handful of regions; ap-southeast-2 is supported but capacity needs to be validated. for pilot we can provision a small pool. we'll need your preferred availability zones and account ids to validate capacity and peering rules

[07:05] Marco: ok, for networking specifics - our VPC uses 10.12.0.0/16, we have a transit gateway already, and we use strict egress rules through nat gateways, do you require specific egress ports?

[07:20] Derrick: typically outgoing ports are limited: control plane uses HTTPS (443) to Redwood control plane endpoints if you're using managed control plane; data plane traffic between your app and our serving subnet is local via ENI, so no public egress for token stream. if you have strict egress, we can do VPC peering + private ip routing or privatelink. we will provide a port/IP list and minimal needed CIDR ranges in the checklist.

[08:12] Priya: another point, we encrypt in transit with mTLS for internal comms, do you support mutual TLS to the private endpoints?

[08:25] Derrick: we support TLS and client certs for certain paths, for the data plane we can enable mTLS between your clients and the endpoint; we'll need to coordinate cert exchange. for control plane there's token-based auth and optional SAML SSO for admin console

[09:40] Ellie: audit / compliance - we need proof of SOC2 and ability to produce per-request audit logs for 24 months, also RBAC and SSO integration

[09:58] Ava: we are SOC2 Type II, we also provide audit logs and can integrate with your SAML IdP for RBAC controls; i'll attach the SOC2 cert and our compliance pack after the call

[11:05] Marco: curious about latency - if nodes are in the same region, what's typical p95 for generation? our use case is near-real-time clinical summarization, under 300ms per request is ideal

[11:22] Derrick: p95 depends on model and token length, for smaller specialized models we see 80-200ms p95 for single-turn requests on dedicated infra; we can do dedicated pools pinned to your account to meet low latency. also batching and kv cache behavior affect latency -- we'll recommend config to meet 300ms SLOs. we should run a benchmark with your payloads

[12:40] Priya: benchmark is critical - we have long context windows too, about 8k tokens sometimes, how does kv cache and long context affect cost and latency?

[12:58] Derrick: for long context we leverage kv cache to avoid re-computing prefixes, but that increases memory footprint. quantization and model variants help cost. we'll provide profiling guidance and cost estimate based on your token distribution. we usually recommend a pilot with representative prompts

[14:15] Marco: back to networking - does Redwood require any inbound rules in our security groups or do you create ENIs in our subnets?

[14:30] Derrick: for privatelink we create interface endpoints which create ENIs in your subnets; security groups will be controlled by you, but we'll provide the SG rules required. for peering there's routing changes and no ENIs on your side, you'll point routes to the peered vpc.

[15:10] Ellie: data residency, if something goes wrong and we need to revoke keys, what's the procedure? and does redwood retain model outputs or logs?

[15:24] Ava: default retention is configurable - enterprise customers can set shorter retention windows, we also support on-request purges. for key revocation with customer-managed KMS you control the keys; if revoked, you'd lose access to encrypted blobs so we coordinate key rotation policies. we'll include those flow diagrams in the security pack

[16:45] Priya: legal question - we need to know about subprocessors and if any model weights or cached artifacts are stored outside our vpc, even temporarily

[16:58] Ava: for private deployments the serving runtime runs in your VPC/subnets and model weights stay on disks in that deployment; control plane metadata may live in our control plane unless you opt for private control plane (an enterprise feature). we'll flag subprocessors in the contract and provide a data flow map

[18:05] Marco: are there terraform modules or cloudformation templates we can use to automate endpoint setup and peering?

[18:18] Derrick: yes we have terraform modules and sample templates for privatelink, endpoint policies, and peering configuration; i'll share those in the follow-up repo link.

[19:30] Priya: costs - what's the rough delta between hosted api and private dedicated? we are concerned about TCO for production at scale

[19:45] Ava: hosted api is pay-as-you-go and easiest but not acceptable for PHI. dedicated/private has a base commit for capacity plus usage; you're paying for reserved nodes plus network and storage. typical delta is higher baseline but lower per-token at scale. we can run a cost model given your projected qps and token counts

[21:00] Marco: on scaling - do you support autoscaling in private deployments, and can we control scaling triggers?

[21:12] Derrick: yes autoscaling is supported; in private deployments we provide autoscaling controllers that tie to metrics and you can set policies. burst capacity options are available but need to be provisioned ahead of time in that region

[22:35] Ellie: any certifications around HSM integration for key storage? we need FIPS 140-2 compliance for key handling

[22:48] Ava: we integrate with customer-managed KMS and HSM providers per region; we'll share the HSM/FIPS support matrix in the security pack.

[24:00] Priya: one more, for VPC peering across accounts, do you require transitive routing changes on our side? we have a hub transit gateway already, would that work?

[24:15] Derrick: transit gateway is usually the best for multi-account setups; peering doesn't do transitive routing by default, so TGW is cleaner. we'll provide recommended architecture: TGW + privatelink for service endpoints or TGW only with direct peering to the serving vpc depending on scale

[25:40] Priya: okay, security folks will want to run the pilot through our assurance program - can you provide a security questionnaire and any third-party reports?

[25:54] Ava: yes i'll drop the security questionnaire, SOC2, and our standard infra diagrams. also will include the bench sheet template for perf testing.

[27:10] Marco: any special IAM roles or cross-account roles needed? we want least-privilege patterns

[27:22] Derrick: there are a couple of cross-account IAM roles if you want us to push logs into your logging account or for S3 delivery; we'll provide the exact role ARNs and minimal perms in the checklist.

[29:00] Priya: how long does a pilot usually take, from infra setup to perf testing?

[29:12] Ava: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 1 infra setup and networking, week 2 provisioning and smoke tests, week 3 perf runs and tuning, week 4 evaluation and decision. timeline can compress if you have people available and regions ready

[31:10] Ellie: do you have a bring-your-own-account option or do you host the nodes in a dedicated account we access?

[31:22] Derrick: we support both - BYOA where we deploy into your AWS account using our operator, or we can provision a dedicated account managed by the customer with cross-account permissions. BYOA is often preferred for full control

[33:00] Ava: ok let's talk failure scenarios - if a node fails or AZ goes down, what are the SLAs and failover patterns?

[33:12] Derrick: we replicate serving pools across AZs within the region and have failover to warm spare nodes; for dedicated capacity we offer an SLA tied to reserved commit. for cross-region failover that's a configuration you can opt into but data residency constraints often prevent automatic cross-region failover

[34:55] Marco: small nit - will we see ephemeral IPs for ENIs that might conflict with existing routing? we plan our IPs tightly

[35:06] Derrick: ENIs will have IPs from your subnets so they shouldn't conflict; we'll work with your ip plan. if you need static ips we can discuss NAT or elastic network interfaces pinned to a small pool

[36:30] Priya: any gotchas with egress charges for privatelink?

[36:45] Ava: privatelink does have data processing charges, but compared to routing across regions it can be cheaper; we'll include an estimate in the cost model.

[38:00] Derrick: quick note on tooling - in the console you'll get token-level breakdowns, latency traces, and model rollouts; for private deployments the console can be in the private control plane or we can send metrics to your prometheus/grafana stack via remote write

[39:20] Priya: perfect, ok final recap?

[39:30] Ava: recap - we will: 1) share SOC2 and security pack + terraform snippets (Ava) 2) share terraform module + endpoint examples (Derrick) 3) Lyon to share VPC CIDRs, account IDs, preferred AZs/regions (Marco) 4) schedule infra deep-dive for peering/privatelink on 2027-07-28 proposed. we'll also run cost model and bench template after we get token distributions

[40:10] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone

[40:13] Ellie: thanks

[40:15] Marco: thanks, bye

[40:20] Ava: thanks all, meeting end

References mentioned: security pack link (link to /redwood/security-pack.pdf), terraform repo (link to github.com/redwood/privatelink-terraform), perf bench sheet (link to sheets.redwood.com/bench-template)
